items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The Scott Brothers, Don Frye and Dickie Wells had New York experience and I was learning more and more about music... It was a good thing to have two trumpet players in the same orchestra with different styles who worked well together in the ensemble.

ctx.x: Springfield was a very small town and there was not much in the line of excitement to interest anyone. That did not worry me but my wife began to miss her friends and relations and we began to quarrel and she decided to go back to Cincinnati, which was the last place I wanted to go back to, to live.

We separated and I moved [in] with a family named Jackson, where Frank Newton and Dickie Wells were staying. Don Frye lived across the street and the Scotts lived two doors from the Jacksons. There was Grandma Jackson, Joldie, one of the grandma's two daughters and Wilhelmina, the daughter of Joldie.

Frank Newton and I roomed together and he became the sweetheart of Wilhelmina and ate with the family. Dickie Wells, Mack Walker, Harold McFerran, John William and myself ate in restaurants. Hubert Mann was married to a Springfield girl and lived with her family.
